SATOM API (REST v1)

SATOM's own REST API for your systems (not the Fortinet device API) — the token-authenticated integration API at /api/v1: how tokens, scopes, capabilities and ADOM binding work, every endpoint, the error format and the rate limits.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage appliances.view registry.view registry.execute_write
📍 WhereBase URL https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1 ; tokens are issued under API Tokens (URL /api-tokens)

Overview#

This is SATOM's own API — the one your systems use to talk to SATOM. It is not the Fortinet device API SATOM uses internally to manage the appliances: that one is described in API registry and API library.

SATOM exposes a small, versioned HTTP API for integrations and automation:

  • Base URL: https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1 — the address of your own SATOM server
  • Authentication: Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request
  • Format: JSON in, JSON out — errors included (never an HTML login page)
  • CSRF: not used on this surface; the token replaces it

The API is deliberately narrow. It can read the appliance inventory, trigger non-destructive scheduled actions an operator created, check an appliance's firmware, and author WAF carve-outs (FortiWeb) or exception rules (FortiADC) from a short allow-list. Since 3.4.0 it also reads and — with explicit capabilities — writes desired state (templates, bindings, baselines), reads what SATOM has observed (configuration history and diffs, the current findings, a read-only metrics query) and runs Plugin Studio apps. It cannot upgrade, flash or reboot an appliance, run any action flagged destructive, or write arbitrary configuration: every write the API offers goes through the console's own path, and a template apply ends in the same dry-run preview and canary-first job as a click in the console.

The whole API describes itself: GET /api/v1/openapi.json returns an OpenAPI 3.0 document built at request time from the live routes, the scope each view enforces and its docstring, so a route is documented the moment it is registered.

In the Network Automation Forum's framework the API is the machine face of the Presentation block, opening onto Intent (/templates, /bindings, /baselines), Observability (/appliances/<id>/config-history, config-diff, /findings, /metrics/query) and the Orchestrator (/actions, /apps, the change-request approval) — see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Tokens#

An administrator creates tokens on the API tokens page (requires users.manage). The token is shown once:

fmk_<public_id>_<secret>

Only a scrypt hash of the secret is stored. A token can be given an expiry in days, edited, or revoked.

Every call is checked against these limits, in order; the first that fails decides the answer:

Limit Meaning
Valid The token exists, is not revoked and not expired
Owner active The user who owns the token is still enabled
Scope read < write < admin; a higher scope satisfies a lower requirement
Owner permission The owner must still hold the permission the scope maps to: read → view, write → config_write, admin → user_manage (see Permissions)
ADOM The token is bound to one ADOM (global, fortiweb, fortiadc, fortianalyzer, fortiauthenticator — those that are active). Queries are scoped to it; a global token may act on any product
Capability Optional allow-list of action types (see below)
AppIDs Optional allow-list of AppIDs that restricts actions to those AppIDs' server policies

A token can never do more than its owner: remove the owner's permission or disable the owner and the token stops working. A token also cannot be created or edited with a scope the owner's permissions do not cover.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a token can no longer be minted or edited with a scope its owner's permissions do not cover, all=1 on the WAF carve-out listing honours admin only when the owner can use it, and raw writes through the internal appliance proxy need registry.execute_write instead of config_write (operators lose them).

Capabilities#

Capability Grants Granted by default?
backend_edit, backend_config, policy_status, cert_swap Scheduled actions that change one server policy (AppID-scopable) Yes, while the list is empty
maintenance, reports Fleet maintenance and report actions Yes, while the list is empty
inventory POST /appliances/<id>/firmware-check No — must be listed
waf_exception_draft, waf_exception_apply WAF carve-outs (FortiWeb tokens or global) No — must be listed
adc_rule_draft, adc_rule_apply FortiADC rules (FortiADC tokens or global) No — must be listed
template_draft (3.4.0) Create templates and versions, bindings and baselines — desired state only, never a device No — must be listed
template_apply (3.4.0) Approve a template (never its own author: four-eyes) and push it through the console's dry-run → canary path No — must be listed
app_arm Run a Plugin Studio app armed through POST /apps/<slug>/run; without it write steps are only recorded No — must be listed

An empty capability list means "any non-destructive scheduled action", but it never grants the explicit-only capabilities — a token minted before 3.4.0 cannot roll a template out or arm an app. A token with an AppID list may only run the four AppID-scopable action types.

On top of capabilities, an app run needs a grant for that very app on the token — one per app, bound to the version an administrator approved (see API tokens). An empty grant list means none. When the object changes, the grant pauses and the call answers 403 grant_paused until it is re-approved.

Endpoints#

Method Path Scope Purpose
GET /ping read Token identity: name, owner, scopes, capabilities, AppIDs, ADOM
GET /appliances read Appliances visible to the token: id, name, kind, host, port, status, last check, maintenance, firmware, model, hardware type
GET /appliances/<id> read One appliance
POST /appliances/<id>/firmware-check write + inventory Ask the appliance for its firmware now and record it (10/min)
GET /actions read Scheduled actions in the token's ADOM, with danger and api_runnable
POST /actions/<id>/run write Run a non-destructive action now (30/min)
GET /actions/runs/<run_id> read Status of a run
GET /waf/exception-types read The WAF carve-out types the API accepts, with fields and required keys
GET /waf/exceptions?appliance_id=<id>[&policy=<name>][&all=1] read Carve-outs this token authored (all=1 needs admin, honoured only while the owner holds the permission admin maps to)
GET /waf/exceptions/<id> read One carve-out
POST /waf/exceptions write + waf_exception_draft (+ _apply to push) Record a carve-out; optionally apply it (30/min)
DELETE /waf/exceptions/<id> write + waf_exception_draft Withdraw an own carve-out from desired state (30/min)
GET /adc/rule-types read The FortiADC rule types the API accepts
GET /adc/rules?appliance_id=<id>&logical=<type> read Live list of those rules on a FortiADC
POST /adc/rules write + adc_rule_draft (+ _apply to send) Preview or create a FortiADC rule (30/min)
GET /system/nodes read, global token CPU, memory and disk of every SATOM node now, graded against the thresholds (60/min)
GET /system/nodes/history?range=<1h…90d>[&node=<name>][&metrics=<list>] read, global token The same readings over time (60/min)
GET /openapi.json read The OpenAPI 3.0 document of every route, built at request time (3.4.0)
GET /templates, /templates/<id> read Templates of the token's ADOM; one template with its body, versions, review history and bindings (3.4.0)
GET /bindings[?appliance=<id>], /baselines, /baselines/<id> read Template bindings and baselines (3.4.0)
POST / PUT / DELETE /templates, /templates/<id> write + template_draft Create a template, add a version (PUT never edits in place), delete (3.4.0)
POST /templates/<id>/approve, /reject, /unapprove write + template_apply The review lifecycle; the author can never approve their own version (3.4.0)
POST /templates/<id>/apply write + template_apply Dry-run preview; with "confirm": true the canary-first background job behind the firmware gate. A fleet rollout needs an approved template and an owner holding Run operations (3.4.0)
POST / DELETE /bindings, /bindings/<id> write + template_draft Bind a template to an appliance with its variables; unbind (3.4.0)
POST / PUT / DELETE /baselines, /baselines/<id> write + template_draft Baselines (template combos) (3.4.0)
GET /appliances/<id>/config-history read (+ config_history on a restricted token) The Source of Truth versions of one appliance: id, hash, captured at, size, source (3.4.0)
GET /appliances/<id>/config-diff?from=<id\|sha>&to=<id\|sha> read (+ config_history on a restricted token) The difference between two versions, secrets stripped (3.4.0)
GET /findings read (+ findings on a restricted token) What the alert engine finds now, scoped to the token's product (6/min) (3.4.0)
GET /metrics/query?expr=…[&start=&end=&step=] read (+ metrics on a restricted token) Read-only MetricsQL over SATOM's own satom_* series only; 10 s, then store_timeout; a product-bound token gets only its devices' series (3.4.0)
GET /apps read Plugin Studio apps the token's owner may use in its ADOM, with their fields and granted
POST /apps/<slug>/run write + a grant (+ app_arm to arm) Run the published version: inputs, armed (default false); answers 202
GET /app-runs/<id> read An app run: status, outputs, steps
GET /builder/target read This server described for SATOM Builder's package rules (see SATOM Builder)
GET /builder/rules-pack read SATOM's package rules (and, from 4.2.0, the test runtime) as a zip, with X-Satom-Rules-Sha256
GET /builder/library read Structure a plugin builds on: datasets and columns, data stores, API Catalog, API library builds (4.2.0)
GET /builder/library/fortinet/<product>/<version> read One API library build's endpoints, or ?endpoint= its fields (4.2.0)
GET /builder/data read + Plugin Studio author This server's rows for the Builder's test data, scoped to the owner: datasets, data stores, satom_select lists; every dataset source (4.3.0, 30/min)
POST /builder/validate write Check a package with the builder rules; writes nothing (30/min)
POST /builder/rehearse write + Plugin Studio author Walk a package's app unarmed, or render a view; installs nothing (30/min)
POST /builder/import admin + super-admin owner Import a package, with the secrets of the connections it creates (30/min)
GET /builder/publishers read The registered publisher keys
POST /builder/publishers admin + super-admin owner Register a publisher key (30/min)

Appliances in maintenance mode are hidden unless the owner may see them; another ADOM's appliance answers 404, not 403.

OpenAPI#

GET /openapi.json needs a read token and returns the document for the routes as registered on this node and release — paths, methods, the scope each route enforces, the capability it declares and a one-line summary from the view itself. A route without a summary is a test failure in the product's suite, not an undocumented endpoint. Nothing is kept in a second list, so the document cannot lag behind the code.

Intent: templates, bindings, baselines#

Reads are scoped to the token's ADOM like a console session and need the owner to hold the Template Library's view permission. Writes need the explicit capabilities above and follow the console's rules exactly: a new version lands pending; approval is four-eyes (never the author); an apply is a preview unless confirm is true, and then the same canary-gated background job behind the firmware compatibility gate; a fleet rollout needs an approved template and an owner with Run operations. The API never writes to a device on its own path. Audit entries carry the token id.

Observability: history, findings, metrics#

config-history and config-diff read the Source of Truth (the actual configuration, version by version); /findings evaluates the alert engine's checks on call and returns the current findings of the token's product; /metrics/query is the only way into the metrics store from outside the node — the store itself stays on loopback with no account of its own. The query must reference satom_* series only (anything else is a 400), answers within 10 s or returns store_timeout, and a product-bound token is handed only the series of its own devices (node series included for a global token only).

Plugin Studio apps#

/apps lists the apps the token's owner may open in the token's ADOM — the console's access list and ADOM rules — with their form fields: each one's help, default (never a password field's), the options a select accepts and, for a list field, the console list it draws from (source; pass the value that list holds — an id for templates and Certificate Manager certificates, a name for FortiWeb objects). POST /apps/<slug>/run with {"inputs": {...}} runs the published version of a granted app in the background and answers 202 with status_url; poll /app-runs/<id>. Unless "armed": true (which needs app_arm), write steps — store writes, writing SQL, non-GET calls, device changes — are recorded as rehearsal: not executed while reads run. A disabled app answers 409 disabled, one never published 409 unpublished, inputs the form refuses 400 app_error. Script apps are not offered.

SATOM Builder#

What SATOM Builder — the separate tool that builds plugins and Plugin Studio apps — calls. Each author uses their own token, so every call runs with that person's permissions and ADOM; SATOM checks every package again with its own rules on validate, rehearse and import. A token whose owner may no longer work in the token's ADOM is refused with 403 wrong_product (target, validate, rehearse, import).

The ADOM of a call. Every Builder call except rules-pack and publishers takes ?adom=<key>. With a Global token it is the ADOM the whole call runs in — the datasets offered, the check, the render and where an import installs — among global and the ADOMs the owner may enter; a token bound to an ADOM may only name its own (403 wrong_product otherwise: it never widens), and an unknown key is 400 bad_request. The target and the library add reach (token_adom, adom, can_choose, adoms) and elsewhere ({"datasets": {key: adom}}: datasets of the owner's other ADOMs, names only). A view that reads datasets of more than one ADOM installs in Global.

Package bodies (validate, rehearse, import) are multipart/form-data: package (the .satomplugin file, at most 10 MB, else 413 too_large) and an optional options field holding a JSON object (else 400 bad_request).

  • GET /builder/target — format (satom.builder-target/1), satom_version, rules_sha256, product (the token's ADOM), caller (username, is_super_admin, scopes, can_author, can_import), choices, templates (the Examples objects a package can never replace), existing (apps, data stores with their columns, connections with has_secret — never the secret —, API versions, scripts), publishers (the enabled ones of this ADOM, with their public key) and schema.
  • GET /builder/rules-pack — application/zip; the header X-Satom-Rules-Sha256 is the zip's SHA-256. The same version always gives the same zip.
  • POST /builder/validate — the package check with the builder policy; HTTP 200 even when ok is false: {"ok", "problems": [{"where", "message", "rule"}], "warnings", "summary": {"kind", "slug", "version", "signer", "signed_by", "creates", "keeps", "needs_secrets", "lands_in"}}.
  • POST /builder/rehearse — options {"inputs": {…}, "answers": "yes" | "no" | "stop"}; the owner must hold studio.script_library (else 403 owner_forbidden). The package is checked first; with problems nothing runs. An app's diagram is walked unarmed (write and script steps recorded as rehearsal: not executed, reads for real); an object the package would create that is not here yet is a problem. Answers {"ok", "status", "steps", "outputs", "waiting", "error", "problems"}; a view or widget {"ok", "rendered", "problems"}. Too many at once: 409 busy.
  • POST /builder/import — options {"allow_downgrade": false, "secrets": {"<connection id>": "<secret>"}}; the admin scope and an owner holding studio.plugin_studio. The console's import path and checks: import rules for a Vision EBC signature, builder rules for a publisher's signature and for an unsigned package. Secrets are stored for the connections the import creates and never logged. Answers {"ok", "kind", "slug", "version", "lands_in", "created", "kept", "todo", "problems", "warnings", "signed_by", "signer", "policy"}; a refusal is 422 package_refused with problems.
  • GET /builder/publishers — a JSON array [{"key_id", "label", "enabled", "created_at"}]. POST /builder/publishers — {"label", "public_key"} (base64 of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key, label up to 80 characters) → 201 {"key_id", "created": true}; the same key again 200 with "created": false; a malformed key or label 400 invalid_key. Disabling a publisher is done in the console (Trusted publishers).

Scheduled actions#

POST /actions/<id>/run runs the action exactly as the operator saved it — you cannot change its parameters. It is refused when the action is destructive (destructive_blocked), disabled (disabled), outside the token's ADOM (wrong_product), outside its capabilities or AppIDs, or already running.

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1/actions
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1/actions/42/run
# {"ok": true, "run_id": 99, "action_id": 42, "status": "ok", "summary": "…"}
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1/actions/runs/99

SATOM node resources#

GET /system/nodes and GET /system/nodes/history return the readings behind SATOM health → Resource history: CPU, memory and disk of the SATOM nodes themselves, not of the appliances.

  • The token must be bound to the global ADOM (403 wrong_product otherwise), because SATOM health is a Global-only page. A token restricted to named capabilities also needs metrics.
  • Node addresses are never in the answer.
  • history takes range (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d; default 24h), node (one node name) and metrics (cpu, mem, disk in percent by default; also mem_used_mb, mem_total_mb, disk_used_gb, disk_total_gb, up). Points are [unix seconds, value], at most 400 per series, each the highest reading in its step.
  • A store that did not answer is 502 store_unavailable, never a 200 with empty series. A bad parameter is 400 bad_request.
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://<your-satom-host>/api/v1/system/nodes/history?range=7d&metrics=disk_used_gb"

Firmware check#

Opens one status call to the appliance and updates SATOM's record. On success it returns the firmware string verbatim ("source": "live", changed, previous). If the appliance does not answer it returns 502 with the last known value and firmware_checked_at and records nothing.

WAF carve-outs (FortiWeb)#

POST /waf/exceptions body:

Field Required Meaning
appliance_id yes A FortiWeb visible to the token
exc_type yes A type from GET /waf/exception-types
wpp_mkey yes The web protection profile the carve-out belongs to
payload per type The carve-out fields
policies for AppID tokens Server policies the carve-out is for
name, reason no Free text
apply no true to push to the appliance (needs waf_exception_apply)
target when applying The device object the entry goes into
create_container no Create the container object if missing

Without apply the carve-out is saved as desired state (an operator applies it on the Exceptions page) and the response includes the exact device plan. The same request twice returns the existing record ("idempotent": true). A template-managed profile is refused (409 template_locked). DELETE removes the record from desired state only; an entry already applied stays on the appliance until an operator removes it.

FortiADC rules#

Allowed types: security_waf_exception and security_dos_exception. Body: appliance_id, logical, mkey (object name), fields (object), apply. Without apply: true the response is a preview of the exact request that would be sent, and nothing is sent. An existing name is refused (409 already_exists). There is no DELETE, and AppID-scoped tokens cannot use this surface (not_appid_scopable).

Errors#

All errors are JSON: {"error": "<code>", "message": "<text>"} (some add errors, allowed or detail). A 401 also carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="satom".

HTTP error When
400 bad_request Body is not a JSON object, or a required field is missing
400 type_not_allowed Carve-out type or ADC rule type not on the allow-list
400 invalid_payload Fields missing or invalid for the type
400 target_required apply: true without target (the record is still saved)
400 unknown_action The scheduled action's type is not in the catalog
401 unauthenticated No Authorization: Bearer header
401 invalid_token Token unknown, revoked, expired or malformed
403 owner_disabled The token's owner is disabled
403 insufficient_scope Scope too low for the endpoint
403 owner_forbidden The owner lacks the permission the scope maps to
403 capability_denied The token lacks the capability (template_draft, template_apply, app_arm, metrics, config_history …)
403 not_granted The token holds no grant for that app
403 grant_paused The app changed after it was granted; re-approve it on the token
409 unpublished The app has no published version
400 app_error The app refused the run (missing input, value not offered, too many runs)
400 bad_request (metrics) The expression references a series outside satom_*, or the range is malformed (3.4.0)
504 / 502 store_timeout / store_unavailable The metrics store did not answer in 10 s / is down (3.4.0)
403 wrong_product The token's ADOM cannot act on that product
403 not_appid_scopable AppID-scoped token on a fleet-wide action or on FortiADC
403 appid_scope_unresolved / appid_scope_denied The target could not be proven inside, or is outside, the token's AppIDs
403 destructive_blocked Firmware upgrade/flash/reboot actions
404 not_found Unknown or not visible to this token
409 disabled / already_running Action disabled / already running
409 template_locked / already_exists Template-managed profile / ADC object name taken
409 busy Too many Builder rehearsals at once
400 invalid_key The publisher key or label sent to POST /builder/publishers is not valid
413 too_large A Builder package is larger than 10 MB
422 package_refused The Builder import refused the package; problems says why
429 rate_limited Too many requests
500 server_error / registry_mismatch Internal error / ADC type cannot be addressed
502 device_unreachable / device_error / probe_failed The appliance could not be reached or rejected the call

Rate limits and auditing#

Endpoint Limit per client IP
POST /appliances/<id>/firmware-check 10 per minute
POST /actions/<id>/run, POST/DELETE /waf/exceptions, POST /adc/rules 30 per minute each
POST /builder/validate, /builder/rehearse, /builder/import, /builder/publishers 30 per minute each

Read endpoints have no specific limit. Calls that change something, and every refused object write, are written to the audit log with the token, its name and its owner. The token's last-used time and address are updated (at most once a minute).

Advanced The internal /api endpoints

/api/… (without v1) is the internal JSON used by the web interface. It uses the browser session and CSRF, not tokens, and is not a supported integration surface:

  • GET/POST /api/appliances, PUT/DELETE /api/appliances/<id>, POST /api/appliances/<id>/test — appliance list and CRUD (the list and Test connection need appliances.view; writes need config_write);
  • /api/fw/<id>/proxy/<path> and /api/adc/<id>/proxy/<path> — pass a REST call through to a FortiWeb or FortiADC (GET needs registry.view and an appliance the user can see; POST/PUT/DELETE also need registry.execute_write, the same key the API-Registry Explorer requires for raw writes, and are audited; appliances whose address is loopback or link-local are refused).

A Bearer token does not authenticate these routes.
